# Arbitrary simplex-container convexification defeats ordinary and paired deficits

## Theorem

Fix d≥2 and put V=1/d!, Γ=(d/(d+1))^d and c_d=1/(16d²).
For every 0<ε≤1/16 there is an actual convex-body mixed source with one
integer coordinate and exactly three full-dimensional continuous fibers
such that:

1. Its summed ordinary fiber depth deficits are at most Γε^d V.
2. EVERY choice of enclosing d-simplices, convexified at the original
   integer bases, adds at least c_d εV mixed volume.
3. The same deficit upper bound holds for paired maximum-depth deficits.

For every n≥2 the example can instead be chosen with no fiber carrying
as much as 2^(−n) of its total mass. The obstruction and its divergent
cost-to-deficit ratio persist. In particular the new ordinary paired-depth
stability theorem does not supply the missing compatibility-cost bridge.

This is a counterexample to that auxiliary bridge, not to (OC).

For a continuous convex body K, let D(K) be its normalized maximum ordinary
halfspace depth and D_pair(K) its normalized maximum paired depth. Write

    δ_ord(K)=|K|[D(K)−Γ],
    δ_pair(K)=|K|[D_pair(K)−Γ].

The ordinary and paired centroid theorems give nonnegative deficits.
The choice of zero shift in the paired infimum gives D_pair(K)≤D(K).
Every simplex has both quantities equal to Γ. All measures below are
ordinary d-volume summed on the actual fibers; hence q=d throughout.

Here the paired definition and centroid inequality are those proved in
`candidate 732b11a769399016`; the paired equality
rigidity for d≥3 is proved in
`candidate d494e7e71949ac0b`. The latter rigidity is
needed only for the optional claim that the deficit ratio has a positive
denominator. The counterexample to a finite cost bound does not require
equality rigidity.

## 1. The actual three-fiber source

Let T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), b=ε², a=1+b, and define

    A={x_i≥0: ε≤Σ_i x_i≤1},
    B=bT,
    P={x_i≤a for every i, Σ_i x_i≥ε}.                         (1)

The change of variables x=a·1−y identifies P with the reflected simplex

    {y_i≥0:Σ_i y_i≤da−ε}.

Thus P is compact, has interior, and |P|=V(da−ε)^d. Also A+B⊂P:
each coordinate is at most 1+b=a, and the coordinate sum is at least ε.
Consequently the convex body

    C=conv( ({0}×A) ∪ ({1}×P/2) ∪ ({2}×B) )                  (2)

has exactly the three actual integer fibers

    K_0=A,     K_1=P/2,     K_2=B.                            (3)

At base 1, grouping the coefficients of the endpoint bases expresses
any hull point as a convex combination of a point of P/2 and a point
of (A+B)/2; both lie in P/2. Extremality of bases 0 and 2 preserves
the endpoints. The projection is [0,2], so there are no further integer
fibers. The endpoint fibers have interior in their d-dimensional planes,
and their distinct bases imply that C has ambient interior. Thus (2)
is an actual convex body, with all three fibers positive dimensional.

Their volumes are

    |A|=V(1−ε^d),  |K_1|=V(da−ε)^d/2^d,  |B|=Vε^(2d).       (4)

The last two are simplices and have zero deficits. For every y∈A⊂T,
some barycentric coordinate in T is at least 1/(d+1). The corresponding
through-y apex cap has T-volume at most ΓV, and its A-volume is no larger.
Therefore |A|D(A)≤ΓV, and

    0≤Σ_j δ_pair(K_j)≤Σ_j δ_ord(K_j)
       =δ_ord(A)≤Γ(V−|A|)=Γε^d V.                            (5)

No centroid is substituted for the maximum in this estimate. The body A
is not a simplex when d≥2: all d coordinate facets and the two facets
Σx=ε, Σx=1 have positive facet measure. Ordinary equality rigidity gives
δ_ord(A)>0. For d≥3 the new paired equality rigidity also gives
δ_pair(A)>0, although positivity is not needed to disprove a finite bound.

## 2. A quantitative nested-simplex lemma

**Lemma.** Let R be any d-simplex containing A, and let L be any compact
convex set containing both R and P. Then

    (|R|−|A|)+2^(−d)(|L|−|P|) ≥ c_d εV.                     (6)

The simplex R may have arbitrary orientation, translation, or size; L
need not itself be a simplex.

**Proof.** Put Δ=|R|−|A|. If Δ≥c_d εV, (6) is immediate. Otherwise let

    η=Δ/V,   δ=η/(1−ε^(d−1)).

Since d≥2 and ε≤1/16, the denominator is at least 1/2, and hence

    0≤δ≤2η<ε/(8d²),          dδ<ε/16.                        (7)

For any point x∈R with x_i<0, join it to the full facet of A in the
coordinate plane x_i=0. That facet is a truncated (d−1)-simplex of
(d−1)-volume (1−ε^(d−1))/(d−1)!. Its cone from x lies in R and its
interior is disjoint from A. The cone volume is

    V(1−ε^(d−1))(-x_i).

It cannot exceed Δ. Likewise the cone from any x with Σx_i>1 over the
full top facet of A has volume V(Σx_i−1), also at most Δ. These estimates
prove that EVERY point of R satisfies

    x_i≥−δ for every i,       Σ_i x_i≤1+η≤1+δ.               (8)

Since e_i∈A⊂R, for each i there is a vertex v_i of R with (v_i)_i≥1.
These d chosen vertices are distinct. If one vertex had two coordinates
at least one, (8) would give

    2−(d−2)δ≤Σx_i≤1+δ,

contradicting (d−1)δ<1. Each v_i has coordinate sum at least
1−(d−1)δ>ε. But εe_1∈R, so a vertex minimizing the coordinate sum has
sum at most ε. It is different from all v_i. Denote it by v_0. These
are exactly the d+1 vertices of R, and

    Σ(v_0)_j≤ε,      Σ(v_i)_j≥1−(d−1)δ   (i≥1).             (9)

For each i, write the point εe_i in its simplex barycentrics:

    εe_i=α_0 v_0+Σ_(k=1)^d α_k v_k,
    α_k≥0, Σα_k=1.

Using Σ(v_0)_j≥−dδ from (8) and (9), comparison of coordinate sums gives

    ε≥−dδα_0+[1−(d−1)δ](1−α_0)
      =(1+δ)(1−α_0)−dδ.

In particular α_0>0, and

    (1−α_0)/α_0
      ≤(ε+dδ)/[1−ε−(d−1)δ]
      ≤(ε+dδ)/(1−ε−dδ).                                    (10)

All displayed denominators are positive by (7). Now fix a coordinate j
and choose i≠j; this is the only step requiring d≥2. The j-coordinate
of εe_i is zero. Since every (v_k)_j≥−δ, its barycentric representation
implies

    0=α_0(v_0)_j+Σ_(k≥1)α_k(v_k)_j
      ≥α_0(v_0)_j−δ(1−α_0).

Combining this with (10), for each j, yields

    Σ_j(v_0)_j
      ≤dδ(ε+dδ)/(1−ε−dδ)
      < ε²/4 ≤ ε/64 < ε/2.                                  (11)

Here dδ<ε/16, ε+dδ<2ε, and 1−ε−dδ>1/2 were used. This argument
allows every vertex and every facet of R to move; no orientation or
contact condition for R was assumed.

The lower facet F of P lies on Σx_i=ε. Its (d−1)-volume is
sqrt(d)(da−ε)^(d−1)/(d−1)!. Since L contains F and v_0, it contains
their pyramid. Its interior is disjoint from P, by (11), and its volume is

    V(da−ε)^(d−1)[ε−Σ_j(v_0)_j].

Thus

    2^(−d)(|L|−|P|)
      ≥ εV(da−ε)^(d−1)/2^(d+1)
      ≥ εV/8 > c_d εV.                                     (12)

For d=2 the last weak inequality uses da−ε≥2−1/16>1.
For d≥3 it uses da−ε≥d−1/16>2, giving the stronger lower factor 1/4.
This proves (6). ∎

## 3. Every arbitrary choice of fiber simplex containers is covered

Choose any enclosing d-simplices R_j⊃K_j, j=0,1,2, and let

    C'=conv ⋃_(j=0)^2 ({j}×R_j).

Its actual endpoint fibers are R_0 and R_2. Its actual middle fiber
K'_1 contains P/2 and (R_0+R_2)/2. Because 0∈B⊂R_2, it also contains
R_0/2. Therefore L=2K'_1 contains both P and R_0. Apply (6); the last
endpoint's excess is nonnegative. We obtain

    Σ_(z∈Z) [ |C'_z|−|C_z| ] ≥ c_d εV.                      (13)

Both projections remain [0,2]. The middle actual fiber may be nonsimplicial;
the lemma specifically permits that. Formula (13) is uniform over all
choices, including nonminimum containers selected jointly to minimize
convexification cost. It also applies if the chosen family is already
compatible and thus unchanged by convexification.

Combining (5) and (13) rules out a finite dimension-only constant times
either summed deficit as an upper bound on this cost. If the deficit is
positive, its ratio is at least

    [c_d/Γ] ε^(1−d) →∞       as ε↓0.                        (14)

If a deficit vanishes, its proposed bound fails immediately. For d≥3 both
ratios are well defined and positive by the equality rigidities stated
in §1. Thus even the new paired-depth simplex stability does not repair
the compatibility-cost bridge in any continuous dimension where it applies.

## 4. An exposed-layer version with no heavy fiber

Let

    F=max{|A|,|P/2|,|B|}>0,
    Q=(F/V)^(1/d)T.

The set Q is a d-simplex of volume exactly F. Introduce a second integer
coordinate k and form the convex body

    D=conv( {(z,0,x):(z,x)∈C}
              ∪ {(z,1,x):0≤z≤2, x∈Q} ).                    (15)

Its projection is [0,2]×[0,1]. Extremality of the k-coordinate at 0 and 1
forces every convex combination in either layer to stay in that layer.
Consequently its six actual integer fibers are

    A,P/2,B at k=0,       Q,Q,Q at k=1.                     (16)

All are full dimensional. The two layer bodies each have relative
(d+1)-dimensional interior, and their hull has ambient interior in
R²×R^d. This verifies the convex-body hypothesis, not merely a list of
prescribed fibers.

The added three simplex fibers have zero ordinary and paired deficits.
Let W be the total mixed volume. Since all three lower-layer volumes
are strictly positive and their maximum is F,

    W=3F+|A|+|P/2|+|B|>4F.                                (17)

Every individual fiber has volume at most F<W/4. Hence no fiber has the
2^(−2) fraction of total mass that would give the simple heavy-fiber
sufficient case.

For any arbitrary enclosing simplex choices at all six bases, the
convexified k=0 section is exactly the convex hull of its three chosen
lower-layer containers. Its added mass is at least c_d εV by (13).
Upper-layer excesses are nonnegative. Thus the full source still satisfies

    total added mass ≥ c_d εV,
    summed ordinary or paired deficit ≤ Γε^d V.             (18)

Finally, for n≥2, take the product with [0,1]^(n−2) in further integer
coordinates. At each binary vertex, extremality prevents mixing with the
other binary layers. All inequalities in (18) are multiplied by 2^(n−2).
The total mass is W_n=2^(n−2)W, whereas each fiber still has volume at most
F<W/4=W_n/2^n. Thus the no-heavy obstruction holds for every n≥2 and
every d≥2. No intrinsic degeneration, missing integer fiber, independent
rescaling of fiber measures, or change in the ambient halfspace family
is involved.

## 5. Exact regression checks

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_all_dimensional_simplex_container_obstruction.py` independently
checks the source inclusion, volume determinants, constants, and no-heavy
inequalities over 72 rational parameter cases. It also constructs 120
independently perturbed enclosing simplices, checks exact barycentric
containment, and verifies all vertex and exterior-pyramid estimates in
the 102 cases falling in the small-volume branch. Every computation uses
rational arithmetic. The proof above is uniform over all d, ε, and
containers; the finite regression checks only test its formulas.

Output: `PASS: 72 exact source/constant/no-heavy cases; 120 independently
perturbed enclosing simplices; 102 small-volume vertex and pyramid
certificates.`
